segments: Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.

Then the Romans assembled,
and set forth with a great force {OCR?} by sea and by land, and reached as far as Kaysum;
and they carried into captivity more than fifteen thousand men, women, and children of the Arabs {Tayyaye}.
And a multitude of the Christian people they took with them by force to the land of the Romans,
lest, they said, the Arabs come and kill them.
And in the year 289
289 of the Arabs, al-Mu'tadid died.
And the magnates sent for his son al-Muktafi,
who was in the city of Callinicus (Raqqa);
and they brought him. Al-Muktafi {OCR?} his son reigned six years and nine months.
He, as soon as he arrived and reigned,
filled up the pits which his father had dug in the ground,
and in which he used to imprison offenders.
This Caliph al-Muktafi had a son whose name was Ja'far;
and he excelled completely in astrology,
so that he surpassed all the ancients.
On one of the days, one of the eunuchs approached him,
having an astrolabe with him,
and said to him:
"Look at the horoscope {rising/nativity} of this child who has just now been born in the court."
And when he examined the horoscope, he said:
"This child has no reason,
and after forty-three days he will take his food with his own hand and eat."
And he said, "Tell me the truth,
what is it?" And the eunuch said:
"In truth, it is the horoscope of the kitten that I brought to you."
And in this same year,
which was the year 1213 {OCR?},
in Homs {OCR: in Homs the city},
there was severe cold,
and the waters froze,
and people wore fur {farrwa?},
and began to warm themselves by fires,
a most wondrous matter.
And in the year 1218,
1218 of the Greeks (907 of our Lord),
Basil the eunuch was sent as an ambassador to al-Muktafi, king of the Arabs, concerning an exchange of prisoners;
and he brought with him ten persons of the Arab prisoners as gifts,
and he was received with honor.
And after a year the exchange was completed,
and three thousand Arab men and women were exchanged,
and were delivered from bonds.
And in that year, which is the year 289 {OCR?: 295},
289 of the Arabs, al-Muktafi died,
and his brother reigned,
[al-Muqtadir] his brother, for twenty-seven years,
thirteen years old.
